content.body: The carve-out in _inbox_rereview_carve_out admits a bot-authored PR past every trust gate (bot-author, draft, author_association, write permission, review mode) based on four checks: repo-native head, a synced+enabled repo config, a tasks-facade run match, and the acting reviewer's toggle. What it never checks is that the PR author IS the identity the self-driving flow uses. The docstring asserts "authorship is forced to the team's GitHub App machine user", but the code does not compare pr.user.login / pr.user.id against that identity. The task-facade match is by pr_url or by (repository, head_branch) — both are branch-name or URL strings that any GitHub App installed on the same repository (or any bot given a colliding branch name on a branch the tasks product also pushed, e.g. a resumed/shared work branch) could satisfy. find_task_run's branch leg matches ANY non-wizard TaskRun with that branch on that repo, including a run whose PR was opened by a different bot on the same branch. If another bot (or a compromised automation with push access to a branch a signals run used) opens a PR whose head branch still matches a signal-report task, this function returns provenance, and the delivery then sails past bot_author/draft/association/write-permission gates and gets a head-pinned auto-approval. Positive identification of a self-driving PR should include the author identity, not just repo+branch linkage.
content.title: Inbox carve-out bypasses the fork and author-trust gates without re-verifying that the PR author is the team's own GitHub App machine user
content.suggestion: Add an author-identity check to the carve-out before returning provenance: compare the PR author's login (and ideally numeric user id, which login renames survive) against the team's Stamphog GitHub App machine-user identity. If tasks records the machine user it pushes as (e.g. on the run or repo config), compare against that stored value; otherwise derive the App's bot login from the installation (the `app_slug` + '[bot]' convention from the installation payload, which the webhook already receives) and require an exact match. Keep the check next to the fork check so the identity chain reads: right repo, right author, right task, right toggle.

content.body: _PR_URL_RE is re.search(r"github\.com/([^/\s]+/[^/\s]+)/pull/(\d+)") with no host anchor and no end anchor. Two consequences: (1) a URL like https://evil.example/?u=github.com/acme/widgets/pull/12 parses as acme/widgets — the receiver leg would then review PR #12 of acme/widgets if the team has a config for it, while the string was never a GitHub URL for that repo; (2) the repo capture group [^/\s]+/[^/\s]+ is greedy across exactly two segments, but because there is no $ anchor after (\d+), URLs with trailing segments (pull/12/files) still match — fine — yet URLs like github.com/a/b/c/pull/12 capture b/c, silently shifting which repo gets matched. The webhook-leg caller passes GitHub's own html_url so shape is guaranteed there, but process_inbox_pr_review consumes a stored string that has already crossed a process boundary, and it is the only validation before a config lookup and a privileged review are keyed off it.
content.title: _parse_pr_url matches github.com anywhere in the string and accepts extra path segments, so a crafted or malformed URL can bind the wrong repo
content.suggestion: Tighten the pattern: anchor the host and the path shape, e.g. re.compile(r"^https?://github\.com/([^/\s]+)/([^/\s]+)/pull/(\d+)(?:[/?#]|$)"), returning (owner, repo, pr_number) and letting the caller join owner/repo. This rejects embedded-host and segment-shifted inputs instead of silently coercing them.

content.body: For a base retarget (`edited` + `changes.base`), the flow is: `_retract_approvals_on_base_retarget` supersedes every non-terminal run and dismisses approvals at every head (with copy saying 'Stamphog re-reviews automatically'), then `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` admits the delivery via `base_retargeted`, then `mode_skip_reason` and the write-permission gate are bypassed, and a new run is created from the SAME payload. GitHub's `edited` payload describes the PR before the retarget is fully recomputed — `pr.base.sha` still points at the old base in this delivery. The webhook path passes this payload's `base.sha` into `build_reviewer_invocation(base_sha=...)`, so the replacement review can run against the pre-retarget diff. For human PRs in LABEL mode this wrong-base review usually doesn't happen (the trigger label is absent), but the carve-out explicitly bypasses the mode gate. The run is also head-keyed and the head didn't move, so the later `synchronize` (recompute push) finds the current head already reviewed by this run and — if the run is no longer QUEUED — does not re-review.
content.title: Base-retargeted inbox PRs proceed on a snapshot whose base differs from what was just reviewed and dismissed
content.suggestion: For `base_retargeted` deliveries, don't create the replacement run from the `edited` payload: either re-fetch the PR from GitHub before creating the run (so `base_sha` reflects the new base), or let the retarget path only invalidate (as it did before this PR) and leave the re-review to the recompute `synchronize`/push delivery. At minimum, assert in the run-creation path that a retargeted payload is not used as the review basis for a carved-out inbox run.

content.body: When a repeat receiver fire finds an existing QUEUED run at the current head, the run's workflow is restarted but its `output.inbox_review` is left as-is. That provenance was stamped from the FIRST fire's `acting_user_id` and toggle check. If the toggle was switched off (or assignment changed) between the first fire and the restart, the restarted run still executes under the stale acting reviewer — unlike the webhook path, which re-resolves the toggle on every delivery. The window is narrow (post-commit workflow-start failure plus a receiver refire), but the restart is the documented recovery path for exactly that failure, and the refire already carries fresh `acting_user_id` it doesn't use.
content.title: Receiver-leg dedupe restarts a stranded QUEUED run but keeps its stale provenance (acting reviewer / toggle state at first fire)
content.suggestion: On the `existing.status == QUEUED` restart branch, refresh the run's provenance before restarting: `existing.output = {**(existing.output or {}), 'inbox_review': inbox_review}` and save it inside the same transaction. That keeps the restart consistent with the re-check-the-toggle-every-time invariant the rest of the PR establishes.

content.body: The PR adds self_driving to the classification dict (line 477) and to the to_dict() audit trail (line 938), but _capture_review_completed (lines 815-855) does not emit it as a stamphog_self_driving property on the stamphog_review_completed event. The hosted server does stamp stamphog_self_driving_review into STAMPHOG_EXTRA_PROPERTIES (products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py), which covers hosted runs through analytics_extra_properties(). Two gaps remain: (1) the engine's own event cannot show whether the flag was on for a run unless the server-side property happens to be present, so any run where the env injection fails or is absent records nothing; (2) the reliability guarantee this PR relies on - Action behavior is unchanged by construction, self_driving always False there - is not directly verifiable from the engine's telemetry, because the engine never records the value it actually used. If a future change ever set the flag on an Action run, no event would show it. For a feature whose safety story rests on default-off and on auditing which gates ran relaxed, the flag should be observable on every review event.
content.title: self_driving flag missing from engine-side review telemetry
content.suggestion: Add one line to the properties dict in _capture_review_completed: "stamphog_self_driving": self.self_driving. This mirrors the to_dict() audit trail added in this PR and makes the default-off invariant checkable with a single query (count events where stamphog_self_driving is true and stamphog_runtime is not hosted).

content.body: The function's docstring defines a reviewable config as one whose connecting user exists, because the sandbox LLM credential is minted under that principal. The query only checks connected_by_user_id__isnull=False. _mint_reviewer_gateway_token additionally requires User.objects.filter(pk=user_id, is_active=True) to find a row, and raises otherwise. When the user who connected the installation leaves the org or is deactivated, the config row keeps its non-null connected_by_user_id, this function keeps returning True, and the Code review scene renders the stamphog_review_inbox_prs toggle as usable. Every queued inbox review then fails closed at token minting. The failure is safe, but the UI flag is wrong in exactly the way the flag exists to prevent: the toggle has nothing to act on, yet it is not rendered disabled. Re-syncing the installation stamps a fresh connecting user, but nothing prompts that while the flag says the repo is connected.
content.title: has_reviewable_repo_config counts configs whose connecting user is deactivated or deleted, so stamphog_connected renders the toggle enabled although every review fails at token minting
content.suggestion: Either join the check to the user table (the facade may read the main DB; a single User.objects.filter(id__in=Subquery(configs.values("connected_by_user_id")), is_active=True).exists() per call is cheap) so the flag matches the token-minting precondition, or document the gap and make the failure visible to the team (for example surface the minting failure on the run so the user learns a re-sync is needed). The first option keeps the docstring's definition of "synced" honest.

content.body: The section says positive identification is "a non-internal, signal-report-carrying TaskRun matched through the tasks facade", and the first rule says "Identification is task linkage, never author-login matching." The implementation in `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py) applies two more identification gates before the facade match: the PR head repo must equal the event repo (fork PRs are rejected because `head.ref` is attacker-controlled on a fork while `repository.full_name` stays the base repo, so a branch-keyed task match could bind an unrelated fork PR to a run), and the repo must resolve to a synced+enabled config (`_resolve_repo_config`, non-blank `installation_id`, `connected_by_user_id` set). The receiver leg similarly no-ops without a synced+enabled config. This file is the contract for agents: it lists the review-mode and author-write-permission gates the carve-out bypasses, but not the fork-safety gate that stops the widened exception from binding an attacker's fork PR to someone else's task run. An agent asked to widen or refactor the carve-out from this doc alone could drop a gate the doc never mentioned.
content.title: Carve-out section omits the fork-safety and synced-repo identification gates
content.suggestion: Extend the identification bullet (or the intro sentence) with the two missing gates: fork PRs never qualify (the PR head repo must be the event repository, since `head.ref` is attacker-controlled on forks), and identification requires a synced+enabled `StamphogRepoConfig` for the PR's repository. Keep the bypass list explicit about what is skipped versus what still gates.

content.body: "Later pushes re-review through the normal webhook path" covers only `synchronize`. The webhook carve-out (`_inbox_rereview_carve_out`) also fires on `reopened` (it is in `_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS`) and on base retarget (`edited` with `changes.base`), and the AGENTS.md section added in the same chunk says "synchronize / reopen / base retarget". A reader of the README could conclude that a close-and-reopen cycle or a base change on a carved-out PR leaves the approval stale, when the code re-reviews those events too. The README and AGENTS.md now disagree on the same trigger set.
content.title: README says "Later pushes re-review" but the webhook leg covers reopen and base retarget too
content.suggestion: Change "Later pushes re-review" to "Later pushes, reopens, and base retargets re-review" so the README names the same trigger set as the AGENTS.md section it points to.

content.body: The receiver reads pr_url from TaskRun.output — a field written by the agent server from observing an LLM agent's actions — and forwards it to stamphog's queue_inbox_pr_review with no check that the URL's repository matches task.repository (repository is already parsed and in scope at line 106, but only used for the branch leg). On the stamphog side, process_inbox_pr_review (the task this dispatches to) stamps inbox_review provenance unconditionally once the team has any synced+enabled StamphogRepoConfig for the URL's repo: it never verifies the PR is bot-authored, never calls find_signal_implementation_run, and never cross-checks signal_report_id or task_run_id. The engine's self-driving carve-out then keys off that provenance alone, so the run skips the bot-author, draft, author-association, and write-permission gates that protect every other stamphog path, and an approve-first review posts a real GitHub approval that can satisfy branch protection. The webhook re-review leg does this identification rigorously (_inbox_rereview_carve_out: bot author, fork check, find_signal_implementation_run match, team recheck); the initial leg does none of it. The PR description states 'a background job checks the PR is really ours (our bot, no fork, the task's repo)' — that check is absent on this leg. Concrete failure: a signals task whose agent is prompt-injected (or simply errs) into recording a human-authored PR URL from the same configured repo in output.pr_url gets that PR an approval-capable review, with the approval attributed to the opted-in acting reviewer.
content.title: Initial Stamphog inbox review trusts an unverified agent-written pr_url, bypassing every approval gate
content.suggestion: Verify the PR's identity before dispatch, on at least one side of the boundary — ideally both. In this receiver, parse pr_url and require its owner/repo to equal task.repository (case-insensitively, mirroring the iexact match stamphog uses) before calling _start_stamphog_review; log and skip on mismatch. In stamphog's process_inbox_pr_review, re-identify the PR the way the webhook leg does: after fetching the PR, require _is_bot_authored(pr), require the head repo to match the config's repository (fork safety), and require find_signal_implementation_run(team_id=team_id, repository=repository, pr_url=pr_url) to return a run whose signal_report_id equals the passed signal_report_id — stamping inbox_review provenance only when all three hold, and no-oping otherwise. That makes the facade safe for any future caller, not just this receiver.

content.body: settings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs is read once in the receiver and the result is baked into the on_commit dispatch. The facade contract ('the caller has already resolved the acting reviewer and checked their stamphog_review_inbox_prs toggle') makes the queued task trust that snapshot. Unlike the webhook re-review leg — which re-checks the toggle on every delivery through resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer — the initial review has no re-check at execution time. A user who switches the toggle off in the seconds between the TaskRun save and the Celery task running still gets a Stamphog review and a potential GitHub approval on their PR. The window is small (broker latency), but the initial leg is also the only one with no webhook redelivery behind it, so a stale read is never corrected. The stale-approval dismissal machinery only fires on later head-changing webhook events, so an approval minted from a stale toggle read can stand if no push follows.
content.title: Stamphog toggle is checked only at dispatch time; the queued task never re-checks it before minting an approval
content.suggestion: Re-check the toggle at execution time inside stamphog's process_inbox_pr_review before creating the ReviewRun: call the registered inbox acting-reviewer resolver (get_inbox_acting_reviewer_resolver) with the passed team_id, signal_report_id, and the run's task_created_by_id, and no-op when it returns None. The hook registry already exists for the webhook leg, so this is a cheap reuse of the same inversion rather than a new dependency. That also hardens the facade contract against any future caller that checks the toggle early.

content.body: find_signal_implementation_run delegates to webhooks.find_task_run. The pr_url leg prefers non-terminal runs but falls back to terminal ones by design (post-merge handling). The branch leg (TaskRun.objects.filter(branch=branch, task__repository__iexact=repository, state__wizard_head_branch__isnull=True).first()) has no terminal-status exclusion and no created-ordering guarantee beyond the default. That is correct for the webhook backstop's purpose, but this facade's caller is a security gate: the stamphog carve-out uses the match to bypass bot/draft/association/write-permission refusals and mint approvals. A PR whose head branch collides with a long-finished (or failed) signal-report task's branch on the same repo still resolves to a DTO here, and the carve-out then only asks whether SOME assigned reviewer is opted in — a preference, not an identity. Positive identification for a trust-gate bypass should bind to the live (or at least recent) run that actually produced the PR, not to any historical run that ever used the branch name.
content.title: Branch-leg task match in find_signal_implementation_run is not scoped to non-terminal runs, so a stale branch name can re-identify a PR as self-driving after the run ended
content.suggestion: For this security-facing lookup, pass a flag or add a dedicated query leg that excludes terminal TaskRun statuses on the branch match (mirroring the wizard leg's .exclude(status__in=_TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES)), and order by -created_at for determinism. Keep the looser find_task_run semantics for the merge-handling backstop; the identification gate wants the stricter shape.

content.body: The PR description states the gate is "at least one of the assigned users has stamphog_review_inbox_prs enabled". The implementation checks the toggle on one user only. `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` collapses the resolved reviewer list to a single acting reviewer (the task creator if they are assigned, else the first resolved reviewer), and `settings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs` is read from that one row. If the acting reviewer has the toggle off but another assigned reviewer has it on, no stamphog review is queued. The same shape applies to the webhook leg: `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` re-checks only that one user's toggle, so after the acting reviewer opts out mid-PR, re-reviews stop even if a second assignee is still opted in. The two toggles are also now coupled through the shared acting-reviewer resolution: a user who wants only the stamphog review (stamphog on, review_inbox_prs off) still blocks both reviews whenever they are the resolved acting reviewer. That may be a deliberate simplification (the ReviewHog run needs a single option snapshot, and the docstring at lines 169-172 describes toggles gating 'the respective reviews' for the acting reviewer), but it does not match the 'at least one of the assigned users' behavior the PR announces, and the mismatch is invisible to users who opted in and get nothing.
content.title: Stamphog initial review is gated on the same single acting reviewer as the ReviewHog review, so an opted-in assignee gets no stamphog review when the acting reviewer is someone else
content.suggestion: Pick one and make it consistent. Either (a) update the PR description and user-facing copy to say the primary assigned reviewer's toggles govern both reviews, or (b) implement the stated any-assignee semantics for the stamphog leg: keep `_resolve_assigned_reviewer` for the ReviewHog run, and for stamphog iterate the resolved reviewers in order and use the first whose `ReviewUserSettings.stamphog_review_inbox_prs` is on (returning that user as `acting_user_id`). Apply the same iteration in `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` so the initial leg and the webhook re-check agree.

content.body: `get_stamphog_connected` calls `has_reviewable_repo_config(instance.team_id)`, which runs `StamphogRepoConfig.objects.for_team(team_id)...exists()` on the default (reader) connection for the stamphog database. Stamphog's own run-gating reads are writer-pinned on purpose: `process_inbox_pr_review` in products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py resolves the repo config with `.using(router.db_for_write(StamphogRepoConfig))` and comments that this is the 'writer-pinned like every read that gates run creation (reader-lag invariant)'. The case that matters here: a user syncs the Stamphog App (a write) and immediately opens the Code review settings; the GET can hit a replica that has not caught up, return `stamphog_connected: false`, and render the toggle disabled right after setup succeeded. The fail-soft `except Exception: return False` makes the same wrong answer appear on any transient read error, so the UI can show 'not connected' for a project that is connected. Impact is limited (a UI flag, and the backend re-gates the actual review on the writer DB inside the queued task, so no review is lost), so this is a consider-level observation rather than a defect.
content.title: stamphog_connected reads the stamphog product DB with the default reader connection, unlike the writer-pinned reads used on stamphog's own gating paths
content.suggestion: Mirror the writer-pinned pattern for this gate as well: in `has_reviewable_repo_config`, route the exists() through `.using(router.db_for_write(StamphogRepoConfig))` (or pin the read in `get_stamphog_connected`), so the connect-then-open-settings flow sees its own write.

content.body: The carve-out (the only place the acting reviewer's `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` toggle is re-checked on the webhook path) runs exclusively inside `if skip_reason is not None`. That guard holds for bot-authored drafts, but not for two realistic delivery shapes of a self-driving PR. (1) `ready_for_review`: the payload snapshot has `draft=False`, and since the bot's app machine user can be recorded with `author_association` MEMBER, `_review_skip_reason` can return None — the carve-out never runs, the toggle is never consulted, and the PR is re-reviewed (and potentially re-approved) even if every reviewer turned the toggle off. The head did not move, so no dismissal path fires either — the stale draft-time approval simply stays. (2) After the PR flips to ready, a `synchronize` payload also trips no pre-filter, so every subsequent push re-reviews with the toggle unchecked. Case 3 in the PR description ('everyone turns the toggle off mid-PR → no review runs') is only guaranteed while the PR remains a draft.
content.title: Webhook path never re-checks the inbox toggle when no pre-filter trips — a toggle switched off mid-PR is ignored on ready PRs
content.suggestion: Run `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` for bot-authored PRs regardless of `skip_reason` (the function already early-exits for human authors, so the extra cost is bounded to bot deliveries), and when it resolves `opted_out=True` on a delivery that would otherwise proceed, treat it as a skip: dismiss any standing approval at the old head with `_INBOX_OPT_OUT_DISMISS_MESSAGE` and return without queueing a run. Alternatively, narrow the documented contract to 'the toggle is only honored while the PR is a draft' and make the receiver leg / UI copy say so explicitly.

content.body: The branch-match leg of `find_task_run` filters on `branch` + repository only; it does not require `output.pr_url` to be empty or to equal the PR being identified. A resumed/retried run whose branch was reused for a second PR (the branch leg deliberately includes terminal runs) can therefore positively identify a bot-authored PR as self-driving even though that run's recorded PR URL points at a different, earlier PR number. The carve-out then stamps provenance (`signal_report_id`, `task_run_id`) from that mismatched run onto the new PR's review. The existing webhook backstop tolerates this fuzziness for follow-up events; the carve-out consumes it as a positive-identification gate, where a wrong binding mis-attributes the review and could admit a PR that no signals run actually produced.
content.title: `find_task_run` branch leg can bind a PR to a run whose recorded `pr_url` points at a different PR
content.suggestion: In `find_signal_implementation_run`, tighten the branch leg before returning a DTO: when `pr_url` was supplied and the matched run has a non-empty `output.pr_url` that differs from it, return None (or prefer the run whose `output.pr_url` matches). This keeps positive identification strictly positive without changing the backstop's matching behavior.

content.body: The self-driving carve-out is documented as covering 'a bot-authored draft PR' (see __init__ comment at lines 202-208), and every inbox PR is bot-authored by construction. But the two relaxations are applied independently: line 225 requires author_is_bot for the bot refusal, while line 590 relaxes the draft prerequisite for ANY PR whenever self_driving is set, including a human-authored one. If the hosted server ever stamps self_driving_review on a context whose PR has a human author (server bug, task-linkage confusion, a human pushing commits that flip authorship signals), stamphog would review — and on the T0 path auto-approve — a human's draft PR, exactly the case the draft prerequisite exists to prevent. The Action workflow's draft gates (.github/workflows/pr-approval-agent.yml) do not cover the hosted runtime, so this engine check is the only draft guard on that path.
content.title: Draft-gate relaxation is not coupled to the bot-authored case it was designed for
content.suggestion: Couple the draft relaxation to the case it was built for, e.g. `if pr.draft and not (self.self_driving and pr.author_is_bot):`. This keeps behavior identical for every real inbox PR (they are all bot-authored drafts) and fails closed if the flag is ever stamped on a human-authored PR.

content.body: With the carve-out, a self-driving PR can now reach APPROVED while still in draft state, and _render_review_body() has no branch that discloses this: the prerequisites gate row renders as '✓ all clear' and no bullet mentions that the approval was granted on a draft. The to_dict() contract records self_driving for the audit trail, but a human reading the pinned GitHub approval or the verdict comment on the PR cannot tell that the draft gate ran relaxed — the outcome looks identical to an approval on a ready PR. Since the approval takes effect when the PR flips to ready, the approving-while-draft fact is material to whoever merges it.
content.title: Approval on a still-draft PR carries no draft caveat in the posted verdict body
content.suggestion: When self.self_driving is true and the PR is draft at verdict time, add a bullet to the review body in _render_review_body(), e.g. 'Reviewed as a self-driving Inbox PR while still draft; this approval takes effect when the PR is marked ready.' This mirrors how the familiarity and assurance bullets already surface review context and keeps the posted record consistent with the audit trail in to_dict().

content.body: get_stamphog_connected calls has_reviewable_repo_config, which queries the separate stamphog product database. The serializer runs this method on every GET of the user settings endpoint (the Code review scene's always-called endpoint, so once per page load per user) and again on every PATCH response, because the viewset returns Response(serializer.data) after a save. The frontend flips each switch through its own updateSettings PATCH, so a user toggling settings generates one cross-DB read per click. The try/except handles the stamphog DB being down (fail-fast circuit breaker), but it does nothing for the stamphog DB being slow: cross-DB latency lands directly on the request path of an interactive settings page, and there is no caching or memoization anywhere on this path.
content.title: stamphog_connected issues an uncached cross-DB query on every settings GET and every PATCH response
content.suggestion: Cache the has_reviewable_repo_config result per team with a short TTL (e.g. 30-60 seconds via Django's cache framework) inside get_stamphog_connected, or inside the facade itself so all callers benefit. Repo connection state changes rarely, so a short TTL costs nothing in freshness. Alternatively, compute it once per request (e.g. stash on the serializer context in the viewset's action) so the PATCH path does not re-query right after the GET-path serialization.

content.body: The fail-soft except Exception returns False for every failure mode, including non-operational ones: a facade signature change, an import error inside the stamphog module, or a bug in the query itself all surface to the user as 'Stamphog is not set up for this project yet' with the switch disabled. The failure is logged (logger.exception), so it is not silent for operators, but the UI state is indistinguishable from the legitimate not-connected state, which makes this class of regression hard to spot from user reports and easy to miss if the log line is not alerted on.
content.title: get_stamphog_connected catches all Exception, masking programming errors as 'disconnected'
content.suggestion: Keep the broad catch (taking the settings endpoint down is worse), but add a metric/counter alongside the log (e.g. ph_scoped_capture or a statsd increment) so repeated check failures are visible on dashboards rather than only in log search. Optionally narrow the catch to expected operational errors (database OperationalError/InterfaceError, circuit-breaker exceptions) and let genuine bugs raise, so programming errors fail loudly in tests and Sentry.

content.body: find_signal_implementation_run delegates to webhooks.find_task_run, whose fallback leg filters TaskRun on branch=... and task__repository__iexact=... Neither column has an index (TaskRun.Meta.indexes covers output->pr_url, state->wizard_head_branch, created_at, task, and team/stage/task), so when the pr_url leg misses, Postgres scans posthog_task_run joined to the task table. _inbox_rereview_carve_out calls this on every bot-authored delivery for a head-changing action on a stamphog-configured repo. Dependabot and renovate PRs never match the indexed pr_url leg (their PRs are not recorded on any TaskRun), so each of their synchronize deliveries pays the full scan. TaskRun is a hot, steadily growing table, and dependabot rebase bursts fan out many synchronize events. What starts as one scan per delivery becomes repeated scans of a large table on the webhook hot path.
content.title: Unindexed TaskRun branch/repository lookup runs on every bot-PR webhook delivery
content.suggestion: Keep the branch fallback off the carve-out path. Inbox self-driving PRs always record output.pr_url on their run (the receiver only fires the PR leg when pr_url is set), so the pr_url leg alone positively identifies them. Add a keyword such as branch_fallback: bool = True to find_signal_implementation_run, pass branch_fallback=False from _inbox_rereview_carve_out, and skip the branch legs in that case. If the branch leg must stay for robustness, add a partial composite index on TaskRun(branch) where branch is not null, matching the existing partial-index pattern in TaskRun.Meta.

content.body: When skip_reason is not None, the code first calls _inbox_rereview_carve_out, which internally resolves the repo config (line 179). When the carve-out comes back empty or opted_out, the skip path calls _resolve_repo_config(installation_id, repo) again (line 891) to run the approval retraction. That is a second identical writer-pinned query per delivery. This path runs for every bot-authored or draft PR synchronize on a configured repo, which is the common case for repos with dependabot or renovate enabled, so the duplicate query is on a hot path.
content.title: _resolve_repo_config is queried twice per skipped bot delivery
content.suggestion: Return the resolved config from _inbox_rereview_carve_out (for example add a repo_config field to _InboxCarveOut, set whenever the lookup ran) and reuse it in the skip path, falling back to a fresh _resolve_repo_config call only when the carve-out returned before reaching the lookup. This keeps one config read per delivery and preserves the deliberate no-enabled-filter behavior of the skip path, since the carve-out's config is the same row resolved by the same function.

content.body: review_hog's receiver re-fires queue_inbox_pr_review on every TaskRun output save that carries the PR URL. process_inbox_pr_review fetches the PR from GitHub before the head-keyed dedupe, because only GitHub knows the current head. An agent run that saves output repeatedly therefore spends one GitHub API call (and one Celery task execution with config resolution) per save, even when the head has not changed and the run will no-op. The installation token's hourly rate budget is shared with the review workflow itself, so a chatty agent loop eats into it.
content.title: Each receiver refire costs a GitHub get_pr call before the dedupe can no-op
content.suggestion: Add a short-lived cache keyed on (repo, pr_number) that stores the last-seen head_sha, checked before the GitHub fetch: on a hit with a live run at that head, skip the fetch entirely. A TTL of 30-60 seconds absorbs save bursts while keeping the lost-synchronize backstop intact, since a genuinely new head still misses the cache after the TTL or differs from the cached sha. The fetch-on-miss path stays exactly as it is.

content.body: On a self-driving run, the author is a bot by construction (the carve-out exists to review bot-authored drafts). The engine still runs _maybe_compute_familiarity on the T1-agent path: on the Action path that is one gh API call plus per-file git blame/log commands over up to 30 files (familiarity.py bounds), and on the hosted path _attach_familiarity runs the same git work from the injected author_pr_numbers. The new _format_self_driving block then tells the reviewer that author familiarity, org membership, and merged-PR history carry no signal for this PR. The result is bounded but unnecessary per-run compute (git blame across the changed files) plus a familiarity block in the prompt whose meaning contradicts the provenance block next to it - a STRONG/MODERATE band for a bot (e.g. a bot whose commits were squashed into these paths before) nudges the reviewer toward leniency that the self-driving prompt explicitly says is meaningless. The pipeline already has the self_driving value at the point both familiarity hooks run.
content.title: Self-driving runs keep computing the bot-author familiarity signal that the prompt then discards
content.suggestion: Skip the familiarity computation when self_driving is set: guard _maybe_compute_familiarity in review_pr.py and _attach_familiarity in review_local.py with `if self.self_driving: return` (pipeline.self_driving for the offline one). That leaves classification["familiarity"] as None, so _format_familiarity renders the empty string and the prompt carries only the provenance block - consistent with the trust story in _format_self_driving and cheaper per run.

content.body: get_stamphog_connected returns has_reviewable_repo_config(instance.team_id), which checks whether the team has AT LEAST ONE synced, enabled StamphogRepoConfig on any repository. The actual review gate is stricter: process_inbox_pr_review (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py) resolves a config filtered by repository__iexact for the PR's own repository and silently no-ops (stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable) when that repository is not configured. In a project where Stamphog is connected for repo A but the Inbox task's repository is repo B, stamphog_connected returns true, CodeReviewScene renders the 'Let Stamphog review your Inbox PRs' switch enabled, the user turns stamphog_review_inbox_prs on — and every dispatch for repo-B PRs no-ops with no signal anywhere in the UI. The only disabled-state copy covers the fully-disconnected case ('Stamphog is not set up for this project yet'), so the partially-connected case is indistinguishable from fully working. The field's own help_text ('at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository') is technically accurate, but the UX it drives promises coverage the per-repo gate does not deliver.
content.title: stamphog_connected is an any-repository check, but the review gate is per-repository — an opted-in user in a partially connected project gets a green-lit toggle that silently never reviews
content.suggestion: The settings endpoint cannot know which repository a future Inbox task will target, so a per-repo flag is not practical here. Instead, set expectations where the user opts in: extend the switch description or the stamphog_connected help_text to state that Stamphog reviews only pull requests in connected repositories (for example, 'Stamphog reviews pull requests in repositories connected to it'), so a user whose tasks run in an unconnected repo is not misled. Alternatively, surface the list of connected repositories in the settings response so the UI can point the user at the gap.

content.body: The fetch failure handler retries every non-rate-limit exception with the 5-second default delay, treating all failures as transient. A 404 (PR deleted, repo renamed or made private, installation removed) and a 410 are permanent: the task burns three retry attempts over the full backoff window and then fails for good. Unlike the webhook path, there is no redelivery behind this leg, and the docstring says the verdict must land while the PR is still a draft for Inbox triage. If the PR never gets another push, nothing re-triggers the review and the only trace is a worker log line, so a self-driving PR can sit at triage with no Stamphog verdict and no signal to anyone that it was lost. The retry posture is the right default for genuine blips; the gap is that permanent failures are indistinguishable from transient ones here.
content.title: Permanent GitHub fetch failures (404/410) burn all three retries, then the one-shot initial review is dropped with only a log line
content.suggestion: Distinguish permanent from transient responses from get_pr: on a 404/410 (or a structured not-found from StamphogGitHubClient), log and return without retrying, since no retry can succeed; optionally capture a posthog event (ph_scoped_capture, per the Celery capture rule) or set a terminal marker the Inbox can show, so a lost initial review is observable rather than silent. Keep the retry-everything behavior for 5xx and network errors.

- **Found:** scenario (2) already behaves as the finding's own suggestion. On a `synchronize` for a ready bot PR, `skip_reason` is `"bot_author"`, the carve-out runs, and an opted-out reviewer yields `_InboxCarveOut(opted_out=True)`. The delivery then enters the skip path at tasks.py:881, `synchronize` is in `_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS` (tasks.py:49), and `_retract_stale_approvals_on_skip` fires with `_INBOX_OPT_OUT_DISMISS_MESSAGE` (tasks.py:894-898). The standing approval is dismissed and no run is queued.
- **Found:** scenario (1) reaches the opposite outcome from the one claimed. `ready_for_review` is not in `_HEAD_CHANGING_ACTIONS` and is not a base retarget, so the carve-out's first guard returns empty at tasks.py:167-168. `inbox_review` stays `None`, `skip_reason` is `"bot_author"`, and the delivery is skipped — the PR is not re-reviewed and cannot be re-approved. That is the documented intent at tasks.py:160-165 and matches the PR description's "Draft becomes ready: no review, and the approval stays".
- **Impact:** no delivery of a self-driving PR bypasses the toggle re-check, and the mid-PR opt-out with approval dismissal already works on ready PRs. The finding is unreproducible against the code as written, so it does not meet the bar.

- **Checked:** the leg order inside `find_task_run`, what `TaskRun.branch` actually holds for a signal-report run, the queryset ordering that decides which run `.first()` returns, and what the mismatched provenance would change downstream.
- **Found:** the branch leg cannot bind a foreign PR, because `TaskRun.branch` never holds the branch a self-driving agent pushes. products/tasks/backend/models.py:651-654 says so directly — the head branch is "Kept out of TaskRun.branch, which means 'branch to check out at provisioning' — not 'branch the agent will create'." Provisioning confirms the semantics with `git fetch origin -- <ctx.branch> && git checkout -B <ctx.branch> FETCH_HEAD` (products/tasks/backend/temporal/process_task/activities/get_sandbox_for_repository.py:348-349). The pushed head branch is stored in `run.output["head_branch"]` instead (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:94).
- **Found:** for a signal-report implementation run the column is the base branch or nothing — products/signals/backend/auto_start.py:253 passes `branch=base_branch`, sourced at auto_start.py:517-519 from `team_config.autostart_base_branches`, which defaults to `None`. A PR whose head ref equals that value is a head-equals-base PR, not a shape a second bot PR takes. So the precondition for reaching the mismatch does not occur.
- **Found:** ordering already prefers the right run. `TaskRun.Meta` sets `ordering = ["-created_at"]` (models.py:1146), so the branch leg returns the newest run carrying that branch, not an arbitrary historical one.
- **Found:** the consequence is narrower than stated. Reaching the branch leg at all means the pr_url leg missed (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:36-59), so no run records this PR. A mismatched bind would then stamp a wrong `signal_report_id` and `task_run_id`. `task_run_id` is never read; `signal_report_id` is used only at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:205 to resolve the acting reviewer, so the effect would be asking the toggle question of the wrong report's reviewers inside the same team — a preference misattribution, not admission of an unrelated PR. The PR still has to clear bot-author, repo-native head (so repository push access), an enabled and synced config, team scope, and a live opt-in (tasks.py:169-178, 201-207).
- **Impact:** the proposed guard is cheap and would read cleanly, but the criteria ask whether the problem can be reached, and this one depends on a branch value the code never produces. That places it in the "speculative what-if" category, so it does not clear the bar.

- **Checked:** the index definitions on both tables the branch leg touches, the gate order that decides which webhook deliveries reach the facade, and whether the pre-existing `find_task_run` call site already paid this cost on the same actions.
- **Found:** the index gap is real. `branch` is a plain `CharField` with no `db_index` (products/tasks/backend/models.py:1081), and `TaskRun.Meta.indexes` covers only `output->pr_url` (partial), `state->wizard_head_branch` (partial), `created_at`, `(task, -created_at, -id)`, and partial `(team, stage, task)` — nothing on `branch`. On the join side, `Task.repository` (models.py:175) has no index either, and `Task.Meta.indexes` lists none covering it. The predicate is `task__repository__iexact`, a case-insensitive comparison, so a plain b-tree index on `repository` could not serve it even if one existed.
- **Found:** the plan is worse than a plain filter because of the default ordering. `TaskRun.Meta` sets `ordering = ["-created_at"]` (models.py:1146), so the branch leg's `.first()` compiles to `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1`. With no usable index for the `branch` predicate, the planner either sequentially scans and sorts, or walks `task_run_created_at_idx` backwards while filtering. In the miss case it exhausts the whole table before returning zero rows.
- **Found:** the fall-through is guaranteed, not occasional, for the named traffic. The `pr_url` leg (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:41-43) is served by `task_run_output_pr_url_idx`, but no `TaskRun` ever records a dependabot or renovate PR URL, so that leg always misses and the unindexed branch leg (webhooks.py:64-78) always runs.
- **Found:** those deliveries do reach the facade. The carve-out's gates before the lookup are head-changing action, bot author, repo-native head, and an enabled synced config (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:167-196). Dependabot and renovate pass every one — they are bots and they push repo-native branches such as `dependabot/...`, so the fork check at tasks.py:176-178 does not stop them.
- **Found:** this is a new cost, not a pre-existing one. The other `find_task_run` call site runs only for `opened` and `closed` — `handle_pull_request_event` returns early for every other action at webhooks.py:153-155, before reaching the lookup at webhooks.py:159. The carve-out adds the same lookup on `synchronize`, which is far more frequent, and rebase bursts fan out many of them per PR.
- **Impact:** every bot-PR `synchronize` on a Stamphog-enabled repo pays a full pass over `posthog_task_run` joined to `posthog_task`, and always finds nothing. `posthog_task_run` grows monotonically, and the Meta's own index comments treat its size as a live concern (the partial `output->pr_url` index exists specifically to stay off "the many runs without a PR URL"). This is the "missing index on a hot path" case, with a concrete trigger and a concrete cost.

- **Checked:** what `_resolve_repo_config` actually costs, how large the table it reads can get, which deliveries really pay the duplicate, and whether repeated calls to this function are new in this PR.
- **Found:** the lookup is an index-served single-row read, and the model documents it as such. `StamphogRepoConfig.Meta` declares `UniqueConstraint(fields=["provider", "installation_id", "repository"], name="unique_stamphog_installation_repo")`, whose comment states "its unique index doubles as the webhook-resolution index for (provider, installation_id, repository)" (products/stamphog/backend/models.py). That is exactly the filter `_resolve_repo_config` issues at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:298-304.
- **Found:** the table is bounded by opt-in. It holds one row per repository that installed and connected the Stamphog App, so it cannot grow with PR or webhook volume. The duplicate is a constant-factor extra point lookup, not an N+1, not an unbounded scan, and not a missing index.
- **Found:** the stated scope is too wide. A draft PR from a human never pays it — the carve-out returns at tasks.py:169-172 on `not _is_bot_authored(pr)`, before the config lookup at tasks.py:179. Only bot-authored, repo-native, head-changing deliveries reach both reads.
- **Found:** repeated calls per delivery are the established shape here, not something this PR introduced. A base-retarget delivery already resolved the config twice before this change — once at tasks.py:858 for the retraction and again at tasks.py:918 on the main path.
- **Found:** the two reads are not interchangeable without care. The skip path deliberately omits the enabled filter — "No .enabled filter: a disabled repo's standing approval must not survive a push either" (tasks.py:892) — whereas the carve-out discards the row when `enabled`, `installation_id`, or `connected_by_user_id` fails (tasks.py:180-186). Reusing it means threading a row past rejections that exist for a different purpose, on a safety-critical retraction path.
- **Impact:** the saving is one unique-index lookup on a small table inside a Celery worker. The proposed fix adds a field to a frozen dataclass plus branching to distinguish "the lookup ran" from "returned earlier". That trade sits in the overengineering category the criteria say to drop, and the cost it removes does not bite at real scale.

- **Checked:** what actually writes `TaskRun.output` after `pr_url` lands, what guards run before the GitHub fetch, how the fetch failure mode is handled, and what the proposed cache would cost in correctness.
- **Found:** the refire is not chatty in practice, because output writes are milestone-grained. The webhook backstop's writer is idempotent and write-once — `_record_run_output_field` returns without writing when the key is already set (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:283-284 and :289-290) — so `pr_url` is stamped exactly once from that path. The other writer is the `set_output` PATCH endpoint, described as "Update the output field for a task run (e.g., PR URL, commit SHA, etc.)" (products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1098). Streaming progress goes through the separate `append_log` endpoint, not through `output`. So a run saves output a handful of times, not in a loop.
- **Found:** a cheaper early-out already precedes the fetch. The repo-config resolution at products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1139-1153 returns silently for any repository without a synced, enabled Stamphog config, so no GitHub call is made at all for teams that never connected the App.
- **Found:** the fetch ordering is deliberate and documented — "The fetch runs before the dedupe because the dedupe keys on the PR's current head, which only GitHub knows" (tasks.py:1157). Rate limiting is already handled rather than ignored: `GitHubRateLimitError` triggers a retry that honors GitHub's own backoff hint (tasks.py:1160-1162).
- **Found:** the proposed TTL cache would reintroduce the gap the design exists to close. The task's docstring states the dedupe keys on the current head so that "a refire after a head the webhook leg never delivered — a lost synchronize — still reviews the new commits" (tasks.py:1125-1128). A cached head sha would make the task treat the head as unchanged for the whole TTL, and the 30-60 second window right after an agent pushes and saves output is exactly when a missed synchronize is most likely. The saving would be bought with the backstop it claims to preserve.
- **Impact:** the confirmed cost is a few extra `get_pr` calls per self-driving PR, on an installation token budget measured in thousands of requests per hour, inside a Celery worker. That is not a performance problem that bites at real scale, and the suggested remedy trades a documented safety property for it.

- **Checked:** the end state a permanent 404 actually produces versus the proposed one, whether a 404 from this endpoint is reliably permanent, which "PR is gone" states are already handled, and what the existing failure trace is.
- **Found:** the two end states are identical. On a permanent 404 the current code logs and retries, then the task fails after `max_retries=3` with `default_retry_delay=5` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109) — no review runs. With the suggested early return, no review runs either. The difference is about 15 seconds of worker time and three extra API calls, not a different outcome.
- **Found:** the observability argument runs the wrong way. Today the attempt ends as a failed Celery task, which is a monitored signal, on top of the structured `logger.exception("stamphog_inbox_pr_fetch_failed", repository=..., pr_number=..., error=...)` at tasks.py:1163-1165. Returning early would replace that failure with a quiet log line, making a lost review less visible rather than more.
- **Found:** a 404 here is not reliably permanent. GitHub answers 404 rather than 403 for unauthorized access to private resources, so this status also covers a token or App repository-access grant that has not propagated. Giving up on the first 404 would drop legitimate reviews in exactly the blip case the code's own rationale protects against — "the toggle-gated initial review has no webhook redelivery behind it, so a transient GitHub blip must not silently lose it" (tasks.py:1155-1157).
- **Found:** the realistic "nothing to review" states are already handled without a fetch failure. A closed or merged PR returns 200, and tasks.py:1166-1169 returns cleanly on it, with the comment noting a late output save can re-fire the receiver long after the PR closed. A 404 needs the PR to be hard-deleted or repository access revoked within moments of the same flow opening it — and a synced, enabled config for that repository was just resolved at tasks.py:1140-1147.
- **Impact:** the change would not alter any outcome, would slightly reduce the visibility of the failure, and risks dropping reviews on 404s that are actually transient. The remaining part of the suggestion — a terminal marker the Inbox can show — is a new surface that does not exist, which is a feature request rather than a defect. It does not meet the bar.
